answer: Each identity posts its answer hash to an atlas board and locks a 60-credit bond, hidden until reveal. Anyone recomputes it against the atlas entry; a mismatch forfeits the bond. Reveals link to the prior reveal, forming an insertion-proof trellis. A copy ring fails: one answer under many identities gives one hash; the atlas keeps the first and slashes the rest. A reused relic answer matches an old hash and is slashed. The k-th fake needs a k-th original text plus 60, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits and 1,000 texts; an honest identity pays 60 once, bond returned after a clean epoch.
